# Modified wallet interoperability peer

The compatibility lane uses **modified** walt.id Wallet API v2 1.2.1, upstream source [cf3c836cc78a9e64b2fd87933527327972e014da](https://github.com/walt-id/waltid-identity/tree/cf3c836cc78a9e64b2fd87933527327972e014da). This is not a claim that the unmodified image interoperates with this profile.

[The patch](preauthorized-only.patch) implements the OID4VCI 1.0 final §12.2 exception allowing preauthorized-only authorization servers to omit `response_types_supported`. Explicit empty arrays and absent/default/code/implicit/mixed/malformed grants remain rejected. Client-attestation challenge metadata remains allowed. Model construction and JSON roundtripping are tested. The issuer advertises only the actual preauthorized grant; it removes unconfigured code, PAR and PKCE metadata.

Patch SHA256: `ed059fd9f91f8b371c2c35839ed5a350185ebea16d346054d286db83e05e73aa`. Upstream license: [Apache-2.0](https://github.com/walt-id/waltid-identity/blob/cf3c836cc78a9e64b2fd87933527327972e014da/LICENSE). The patch is supplied under this repository's Apache-2.0 license; it has not been published as an upstream contribution or public image. The upstream [notice](NOTICE.md) is retained verbatim. Preserve upstream license and third-party notices when redistributing source, jars or images; this repository's license does not replace dependency licenses.

Build the exact public source and run its real JVM test suite, then package its complete `installDist` runtime in the digest-pinned image:

```sh
node vendor/waltid/build-peer.mjs
```

This needs Docker, Git, network access, several GB of temporary disk space and enough memory for the upstream JVM build. Both builders cap the Gradle daemon (including the in-process Kotlin compiler) at 4 GiB; forked test JVMs and native memory require additional headroom. It creates `credspan-wallet-peer:1.2.1-preauth` locally and prints its image ID and temporary source/log directory. It never mounts the Docker socket into a container. The upstream build may warn that Kotlin/Native publishing is unsupported on Linux arm64; only JVM tests and the wallet service distribution are requested. Build logs and upstream code remain outside this repository. First build can take more than ten minutes.

CI can reuse an input-qualified tested runtime distribution before assembling the same digest-pinned image. See [CI verification and cache trust boundaries](../../docs/ci.md) for key inputs, validation, main-only writes and optional local use.

Build failures emit a bounded `peerBuildFailure` JSON diagnostic into the CI log before throwing: fixed stage, UTC/elapsed time, numeric exit status, validated signal/error code, observed output sizes and default-deny classified tail categories. Arbitrary command output, URLs, paths, environment and error messages are never copied into that report. A category records an observed message pattern, not a proven root cause (for example, SIGKILL alone does not establish OOM). Raw stdout/stderr remains only in the private temporary build directory; it is not automatically uploaded. The sanitized report survives loss of that directory through the hosted job log. No retry, timeout or resource policy was changed.

## Private hosted variant

The [hosted wallet Dockerfile](../../ops/hosted/Wallet.Dockerfile) uses the same exact upstream source and preauthorized patch, plus [access.patch](access.patch), SHA256 `d749318eda575f40399b9338814496753935a733cc9a965b138cc4ea151eff9f`. That second modification confines service credentials to the exact configured HTTPS API origin, disables redirects and HTTP header logging, and adds a JVM boundary test. Both builders additionally apply [dependencies.patch](dependencies.patch), SHA256 `32cb0096a32693e17674038caa316605822c4b879e9cf5fad41008ea50b33041`. It aligns the actual service runtime with the source catalog’s Netty 4.2.19 and Jackson 2.22.4 patch families and selects Guava 33.8.0-jre, PostgreSQL JDBC 42.7.14, Vert.x 4.5.35, JSON 20260719 and Rhino 1.7.15.1. Both builders run the preauthorized protocol and wallet service tests and package the complete source-resolved `installDist` libraries; the hosted variant also runs the Access boundary test. They remove the previous `/app` payload before installing the new jars and exclusive classpath in the generated launcher's service-first order, retain upstream notices and jar licenses, and install the exact Ubuntu 26.04 apt/libapt, glibc, PCRE2 and Perl security revisions listed in [dependency patches](../../docs/dependency-patches.md). The local builder applies the preauthorized and dependency patches; only the hosted variant adds Access. This does not qualify unused wallet ecosystems or every transitive library path.

These modifications do not fix upstream wallet CORS or all upstream dependency findings. The [hosted runbook](../../docs/hosted-sandbox.md) requires the wallet Origin WAF rule as well as Access and private ingress. See [known security limits](../../SECURITY.md) before using or redistributing this peer. The upstream [THIRD-PARTY-NOTICE.md](https://github.com/walt-id/waltid-identity/blob/cf3c836cc78a9e64b2fd87933527327972e014da/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICE.md) and packaged `META-INF/NOTICE.html` files identify upstream third-party components.
